extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media relations practitioners, and PR professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A standard corporate/organizational press release announcing an event/award shortlist, showing the conventional structure and elements a PR release should include (headline, dateline/lead, key facts, logistics, links, boilerplate, contacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA Announces Shortlist for 2022 Anvil Awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, declarative title that summarizes the news. Typically placed prominently at the top and should convey the main announcement (who + what). May include the organization's name or the event/award name for immediate clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and lead
rubrics_metrics.description: March 17, 2022 – PRSA, the nation’s leading professional organization serving the communications community, announced today the shortlist for the 2022 Anvil Awards, which recognize and honor the very best communications programs planned and executed each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a dateline (date and, optionally, city) followed by an opening sentence that identifies the organization and summarizes the news (who, what, why). Common format: 'Month Day, Year – Organization, [brief identifier], announced...' This lead frames the release for journalists and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of scope and key facts
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 151 campaigns across 65 categories and subcategories have been named to the shortlist, comprising Silver Anvil and Bronze Anvil entries, including submissions from leading brands, agencies, non-profit organizations, government agencies and universities. The most entered categories include Integrated Communications, Media Relations, Events and Observances, Media Relations and Community Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present quantifiable and newsworthy details (counts, categories, types of entrants, notable trends). Highlight the most relevant specifics journalists will use in coverage. Use short sentences and concrete numbers to convey importance and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event logistics and award process details
rubrics_metrics.description: This year’s ceremony, which will include the presentation of both Silver Anvil and Bronze Anvil Awards, will be held on May 19th at the New York City’s Edison Ballroom. From each Anvil category’s shortlist, one Anvil winner and up to one runner-up will be announced during the event. The “Best Of” Silver Anvil will also be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear information on when/where any related events will occur and how awards/winners will be determined or presented. Journalists need date, location, and what will happen (presentations, winners, special awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action / links to additional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Click here to R.S.V.P. and view the schedule of the evening's festivities. The complete shortlist can be found here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include actionable links or directions (RSVP, full lists, schedules, press kits). Make it easy for reporters to find supplementary materials; label links clearly (e.g., 'complete shortlist', 'RSVP', 'press kit').

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate / About paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: About PRSA: The Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) is the nation’s leading professional organization serving the communications community. PRSA is the principal advocate for industry excellence and ethical conduct and provides members lifelong learning opportunities and leading-edge resources to enhance professional connections and support them at every stage of their career. With nearly 30,000 members, PRSA is collectively represented by 110 Chapters and 14 Professional Interest Sections, and on nearly 375 college and university campuses through its student organization, the Public Relations Student Society of America (PRSSA). For more information, please visit www.prsa.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a short boilerplate describing the organization (mission, size, structure, website). This standardized paragraph provides background for reporters and can be reused across releases.

rubrics_metrics.description:

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide named media contacts (names, titles) and organizational contact details (address, phone/email if available). Ensure contacts are current, reachable, and positioned to respond to media inquiries; include multiple contacts if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-release marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a conventional end marker (### or -30-) to indicate the official end of the press release copy so journalists know no further release text follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise paragraphing and clear structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The release uses short paragraphs each focused on a distinct point: announcement, supporting facts, event logistics, links, boilerplate, contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the release into short, single-idea paragraphs for readability. Start with the most newsworthy material, then supply supporting details, quotes (if present), logistics, links, boilerplate, and contact info. Avoid long dense paragraphs.
